title: schedule -- Prompt Scheduler Cheatsheet (add/list/remove/pending)
desc: Full reference for wkappbot schedule: one-shot/recurring/limit-reset JSON schedules + file-based pending_prompts. Two-layer scheduler system.
steps: TWO LAYERS: (1) schedule add/list/remove → JSON ScheduleManager file (global, schtasks-backed). (2) schedule pending list/delete → .wkappbot/pending_prompts/ files per CWD (filename-encoded, zero-memory). Layer 1 = system/global triggers; Layer 2 = project-scoped recurring prompts.
ADD ONE-SHOT: wkappbot schedule add --at HH:mm --prompt 'text'  |  --at 30m (relative)  |  --at 2026-05-01T09:00 (ISO). Registers Windows schtasks entry -- survives Eye kill/restart.

ADD RECURRING: schedule add --every 20m --prompt 'text' [--max-runs N] [--expires HH:mm]. --every-day HH:mm for fixed daily. --on-limit-reset fires on Claude rate-limit reset. --cmd 'python script.py' (bash/python auto-resolved on Windows). --prompt-file ./path.md reads prompt from file.

LIST/REMOVE/CLEAR (Layer 1): schedule list -- id, status (pending/done/failed/expired), next time, interval, run count. schedule remove <id>. schedule clear [--pending]. schedule exec <id> -- manual trigger (called by schtasks).

PENDING LIST (Layer 2): wkappbot schedule pending list [--cwd <path>]. Shows: next trigger local time + rep/tod/days params + filename. Default cwd = current dir. No cwd arg needed if already in project root.

PENDING DELETE (Layer 2): schedule pending delete <pattern> [--cwd <path>]. Pattern = substring OR glob (* ?). --all removes everything. THE ONLY WAY to cancel infinite rep= (no cnt=) schedules. Ex: schedule pending delete quant20m --cwd D:/GitHub/WkAutoQuant

FILENAME SCHEMA (Layer 2): prompt_{utcYYYYMMDDHHMMSS|NOW}_{label}[,rep=Nh|Nm|Ns][,cnt=N][,tod=HHMM-HHMM][,days=weekdays|weekends|mon-fri|1-5|mon,wed,fri].json. tod+days = local-time window gate. Outside window: skip delivery + silent reschedule. See: file-as-scheduler-pending-prompts-pattern

EXAMPLES: schedule add --every-day 09:00 --prompt TEXT | schedule add --on-limit-reset --prompt TEXT | schedule add --every 30m --max-runs 5 --prompt TEXT | schedule pending delete --all --cwd D:/GitHub/WkAutoQuant | KR market file: prompt_NOW_quant,rep=20m,tod=0900-1530,days=weekdays.json

SCHEDULE INJECTION LESSONS (2026-05-01, commits d386cd01 + fb8861e5): (1) TargetHwnd stored at schedule-add time is the correct primary target. EnumerateAllTerminalWindows picks the WRONG Claude session when multiple project Eyes run simultaneously. Fix: always add storedHwnd as FIRST candidate before cache/enumerate. (2) TargetHwnd is a string? in ScheduleItem (JSON hex string, e.g. '2B083E'), NOT IntPtr -- must parse via long.TryParse(hex, NumberStyles.HexNumber) then new IntPtr(val). (3) My fix was silently removed by a subsequent code restructure (3c527b48). When injection code is refactored, verify TargetHwnd-first logic survives. (4) JSONL-verify strategy (multi-candidate with 5s verify) is correct for fallback but TargetHwnd must come BEFORE cache and enumerate to be useful.

WINDOWS TERMINAL TAB TARGETING (2026-05-02 discovery): Each WT tab has its OWN top-level CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS hwnd -- NOT shared. Example: 0x2B083E='Claude Code wkappbot-sdk', 0x3044E='PowerShell', 0x131E8C='WkAutoQuant'. Confirmed via EnumWindows: 5 separate CASCADIA windows all pid=16132 (same WT process). Gemini said 'tabs have no hwnd' -- WRONG. Each tab IS its own CASCADIA window. KEY: GetForegroundWindow() returns the EXACT tab hwnd when user types from that WT tab. So at schedule-add time, fg=CASCADIA of the registering tab = correct TargetHwnd. CWD-BASED DYNAMIC LOOKUP: wkappbot a11y find {cwd:'D:/GitHub/project',hwnd:''} returns the subordinate PseudoConsoleWindow (child of the correct CASCADIA tab). From that PseudoConsoleWindow, walk up to find the parent CASCADIA = correct tab hwnd. This enables CWD-based dynamic targeting at execution time -- no stale TargetHwnd needed. CHAIN: find({cwd:'...'}) -> PseudoConsoleWindow -> GetParent(CASCADIA) -> SetForeground -> inject. grap hwnd:'' field forces hwnd to appear in find output -- otherwise hwnd is hidden.
